chapter: Jamming, bootleg records and the Topsy hit
title: How 'Topsy' began: the backer at the Metropole
summary: A young man at the Metropole asks him to record a number; Cole improvises 'Topsy' as the title.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did you ever have that trouble with 'Topsy'?
Not the bootlegging. See, with 'Topsy,' I'll tell you how that came about. I was in the Metropole with

my band at the time. During that same period I was doing the Arthur Godfrey show. At night, I would come there at the Metropole and work. Well, one of those evenings at the Metropole this young man came in with his date and I happen to be doing 'Caravan' with the fluorescent sticks and things, and he liked it, you know.

And he was there sitting with his date, drinking. Called me over to the table. 'Cozy, I'm so and so, this is my date, I'm going to marry her, I'm in love with her'. So you're used to those kind of stories, you know. And drinking, too. I said, oh it's a pleasure, wish you every happiness. He said 'Cozy, I'd like for you to record that number for me, 'Carmen', I mean 'Caravan.' And I says okay. I says, but the thing of it is about, I mean the truth of the matter everybody has done 'Caravan,' Duke, every band,' I says, 'you come back in a couple more days and I'll think of a number.' I didn't have any number in mind. I always figured that maybe that was one of those one night stands.

So anyway, a couple of nights he came by. And he said, Cozy, I'm back again. I says okay, how are you, you know. I said I've got a number for you, and just off the top of my head, not thinking, I said 'Topsy.'
